newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Telecom merger highlights trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Telecom merger highlights trade.

text.p: Options investors took profits in MCI Communications Corp, bargain-hunted in AT&T Corp and played both sides of British Telecommunications Plc, traders said Monday.
Over the weekend, MCI and British Telecom agreed to merge in a whopping $21.5 billion deal. Analysts said AT&T would face stiff competition from the new company.
MCI topped the over-the-counter actives list, as did AT&T on the NYSE. By 1030 CST (1630 GMT), MCI shares were up 1/2 at 30-3/4 on more than 18 million shares. The stock had reached a high of 33-1/4.
At the same time, AT&T was off 3/4 at 33-3/4 on consolidated volume of 5.12 million shares. It hit an intraday low of 33-1/4, a new 52-week low.
ADRs of British Telecom surged 5-3/4 to 61-1/4 on about 1.15 million shares, more than four times its daily average.
The rally in BT shares increased the value of the merger to around $21.5 billion from $20 billion.
Traders said last Friday that investors had been snapping up MCI calls over the prior week but analysts said the trading pattern did not indicate insider trading.
Some of those positions were being unwound on Monday.
"They're selling the deep-in-the-money calls and selling some strangles," one trader said of MCI options action.
He cited the January 30-32-1/2 strangle as an example of what investors were selling.
The January 30 put traded more than 1,300 contracts by 1045 CST (1645 GMT) and the January 32-1/2 call traded about 1,800 contracts.
Most of the sellers were institutional investors.
Some investors were buying some of the out of the money calls such as the November and December 35s, which traded 200 and 300 contracts, respectively.
Volatility in MCI options declined to normal levels around 30, traders said. It had surged last week amid the heavy call buying.
Traders said most activity in AT&T options was investor buying.
"People are looking at this as a buying opportunity," one trader said. "The options are pretty cheap.
"We had options five dollars in the money trading for one dollar," he added. "So a lot of people are looking at this as a good spot to step in and buy."
The trader said volatility increased only slightly on AT&T options.
The December 35 call was most active, with more than 1,700 contracts changing hands. It eased 7/16 to 1-1/16.
Other actives included the November 35 all and the November 30 and 35 puts.
In British Telecom options, traders said institutions were the major participants, buying and selling calls and puts.
The British Telecom November 60 call traded about 1,175 contracts and the corresponding put traded about 1,135. -Gregory Crawford, 312/408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
